Amazon S3 Glacier is a secure, durable, and extremely low-cost cloud storage service for data archiving and long-term backup. It is designed to deliver 99.999999999% durability, and provides comprehensive security capabilities. Customers use Glacier to store data long term, while having the flexibility of retrieving their data within a few minutes (using expedited retrieval speed) or few hours (using standard or bulk retrieval speeds.) Conventional storage systems are a poor fit for this domain as they are typically optimized for speed rather than space and cost. Glacier's unique constraints lead to to fascinating scaling and algorithmic problems that have never been tackled at our scale. To meet our cost goals, we have a constant need to drive fundamentally new storage technologies in the industry and come up with innovative ways to further optimize costs. We are now working on the next set of major hardware and software enhancements to the service and are seeking a Software Development Engineer to join our rapidly growing team.
As a developer on our team, you'll have the opportunity to lead the design and implementation of a distributed storage service that operates at extreme scale. Your design and development work would range from distributed system service development in Java, to low level systems coding that interfaces directly with hardware. You'll operate on the bleeding edge of innovations in the storage field, and will need to solve challenging fundamental computer science problems.
We are looking for a seasoned engineer who is keen to lead, invent in this space, and build what could easily become the largest data storage service on the planet.
Our team works together to provide work/life balance for all team members. We recognize that the circumstances of our team members vary, and we balance work across the team so that we’re all able to maintain high standards on behalf of our customers, while at the same time allowing for rich and happy personal lives.
In AWS, if you build it, you own it. Amazon S3 Glacier is a highly available 7x24 worldwide service requiring dedicated support from our engineering teams. We pride ourselves on a high level of ownership in the work we do. This means we hold a high bar for test automation, verification processes, design and code reviews to ensure that our systems meet the exacting standards our customers demand. We maintain a regular on-call rotation across our teams with engineers and managers all taking part to resolve the inevitable issues that arise. We work hard to minimize getting paged in the middle of the night as we recognize that a well-rested employee is a productive employee.
Upon joining Amazon S3 Glacier, every employee is paired with a peer buddy who will help you to quickly come up to speed in understanding the technology we’re building, the tools we use and the business problems we’re trying to solve. We hire exceptional people and we recognize the importance of coaching others. We have a formal mentor search application that lets you find a mentor that works best for you based on location, job family, and job level. On our internal “Broadcast” video streaming website, you’ll find countless presentations by some of the brightest minds in computing discussing solutions to many of the exciting problems we’re solving in AWS today with new live-streaming videos added every week.
Work/Life Balance
Our team puts a high value on work-life balance. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. Who are we?
Annapurna Labs is the part of Amazon that designs the custom silicon behind the cloud, including Trainium for AI training, Graviton CPUs, and the AWS Nitro system. Nearly every server in AWS runs hardware we designed. We're a new team inside Annapurna Trainium Systems taking Trainium beyond AWS, so customers can run it in their own data centers.
What do we do?
We build the software that runs on Trainium servers in customers' own data centers. We also build the software customers use to install, provision, operate, update, and monitor those servers. We give the people who run this hardware a complete way to stand it up, watch its health, deliver new software to it, and diagnose it, all through open, standard interfaces. We own that software from design through the running system.
Why it's high-impact?
The hardware is just silicon until our software makes it provisionable, observable, and serviceable. Every system runs through what we build. The service you own is on the path for all of them, and the people who run this hardware depend on it every day.
What's the challenge?
There are many ambiguous and difficult challenges in our fast-moving space. Our services require deep system and software expertise. You need to have the ability to work within a fast moving and startup-like environment in a large company. You will identify solutions, trying ideas, given space to fail and iterate to produce products that your customers love.
What you will do?
You own a large component of the software that manages servers, racks, and clusters from outside. Do you want to own Identity systems that major AWS and Stores services depends on to exist and the layers that make that data consumable by every service that needs it? The LDAP Core and Switchboard teams are part of the AFSS Identity organization within Amazon's Foundational Security Services. We hold the records of engineering identity at Amazon, and we make that record reachable through modern access pattern.
LDAP Core operates the canonical engineering identity directory: the 389DS LDAP fleet, its global replication topology, and the regionalized architecture (REGAL) we are building to replace it by 2027. Switchboard builds the routing, temporal, analytical, and control layers that surround that directory the Read Proxy, Time Machine, the Identity Data Lake, and GSAM, the control plane for millions of system accounts across Amazon's engineering data planes.
Key job responsibilities
- Lead the REGAL regionalized architecture: read/write fleet split, Regal Replicator, and ORR through full partition coverage
- Own 389DS software lifecycle: upgrade train, master fleet replication, schema management across commercial, GovCloud, ADC, China, and MVP
- Drive pipeline-driven automated region builds, eliminating manual ceremony from partition expansion
- Lead schema evolution discipline: document every attribute, analyze consumer impact end-to-end before every change
- Architect and evolve the LDAP Read Proxy: schema-routed access, expansion to BRASS and additional backends, transparent to existing callers
- Own GSAM as the system-account control plane across LDAP, POSIX, ANT : lifecycle management, credential rotation, ANT auto-provisioning, and the path to passwordless system accounts
- Own LDAP Time Machine and the Identity Data Lake: snapshot pipelines, S3 vending, cross-region log analytics, and IdP security intelligence
- Set the observability standard across every access path -direct, proxied, historical, analytical, consistent telemetry, uniform authorization
- Serve as Tier-1 on-call anchor for directory availability and replication health
- Mentor engineers and raise the technical bar across both teams
A day in the life
You'll start by reviewing system metrics and addressing any operational issues affecting our Identity services. Throughout the day, you'll collaborate with Identity and Access Management service teams to design features, participate in architecture reviews for scalability improvements, and write high-performance code to handle authentication and authorization requests across Amazon's services. You'll also mentor team members through code reviews and contribute to strategic planning for next-generation identity systems.
